clue.text: Standard model used to be more than enough

parts.note: an ex is something that used to be, as in ex-wife
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: A former standard model, perhaps of a car, that was once more than adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern or exemplar others are measured against, a standard to copy.

clue.text: Employ criminal gang to get into drugs

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within another
criminal suggests crooked, so the letters of the word beside it are bent out of order

parts.note: E is ecstasy; the plural gives two of them, one each side
the four letters of gang rearranged
the second ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A boss hires a criminal gang to move into the drugs trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Drugs is read as E plus E, two ecstasy tablets, with the rearranged gang between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them, as you would employ staff.

clue.text: Have enough money for a fine car

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they can pay for a nice car.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to be able to pay for it, a straight synonym phrase.

clue.text: Ownership of society's work is returned before hearing

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society; the 's ties it to the next word
OP, short for opus, is a work
a court sits in session to hear a case

explanation.surface: A legal dispute over who owns a society's work, handed back before the court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Possession is the state of having or owning something, a plain synonym for ownership.

clue.text: Bear up having hard time

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: to cope with something is to bear it
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Encouragement to someone struggling through a difficult period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard time' looks like one phrase, but hard gives a letter and time alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long historical period, a stretch of time.

clue.text: Mum abandoning vernacular is silly

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters drop out

parts.note: idiomatic language is natural, everyday vernacular
Ma is mum; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Dropping your mother tongue is a foolish thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic behaviour is stupid or foolish, a direct synonym of silly.

clue.text: It's not fair raising tax on only one church

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer; the answer is a noun for an unfair thing

indicators.note: raising lifts something upward, which in a down entry reads it bottom to top

parts.note: NI is National Insurance, a UK payroll tax
just means only
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tax rise falls on a single church alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An injustice is an unfair act or situation, exactly what is described as not fair.

clue.text: Native American states

parts.note: IN is the postal code for Indiana
CA is the postal code for California

explanation.walkthrough: One word, states, supplies two US state abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were an indigenous people of South America, so an Inca is a Native American.

clue.text: At Dior "Le Fashion" is specially cut

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the preceding letters are remade in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, taken together

explanation.surface: A Paris fashion house's look described as bespoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Fashion looks like part of the brand name in quotes, but as a verb it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailored clothes are cut to fit a particular person, made specially for them.

clue.text: Building material originally cast on Greek island

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of cast
taken as written
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Building material first poured on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete is the cement, sand and aggregate mix used in construction.

clue.text: Model in picture files has talents

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: GIFs are a common image file format
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A fashion model whose photos online show real ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts are natural aptitudes, the same as talents.

clue.text: 1-0 given at last after goal protest

parts.note: an object is an aim or goal
the numerals read as the letters I and O

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of given

explanation.surface: A team at 1-0 down protests after a late goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Goal is a football score in the surface, but here it means aim. The pieces are placed with goal first, as after directs.
explanation.definitionFit: An objection is a formal protest against something.

clue.text: Used to water oranges he'd cultivated

definitions.note: a description; the answer is the thing used to water

indicators.note: cultivated ground is worked over, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, taken together

explanation.surface: A grower watering the orange trees he has raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is the flexible pipe people use for watering plants.

clue.text: Fell in low river

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled into a shallow river.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell reads as a past tense verb, but it is the noun: in northern England a fell is a stretch of upland.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell and a moor are both open, uncultivated hill country.

clue.text: Depression about husband's evident everywhere

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a trough is a dip or depression
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's means 'is'
something out is in the open, plain to see

explanation.surface: A husband's depression is plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means in every part, the same as everywhere.

clue.text: Is the Queen arriving in Birmingham university hospital dept causing surprise?

parts.note: Aston is a university in Birmingham
taken as written
HM stands for Her Majesty
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Would a royal visit to a Birmingham hospital department cause a stir?
explanation.walkthrough: Arriving in tells you the Queen's piece follows the university's.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is a feeling of great surprise.

clue.text: Pushy old boy has unexpected virtues

indicators.note: unexpected suggests things turning out differently, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the letters of virtues rearranged

explanation.surface: An assertive former pupil turns out to have surprising good qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtrusive means intrusively prominent, forcing itself on others like a pushy person.

clue.text: Woodcutter bonds with a wife

parts.note: chains are bonds or fetters
with is a joining word; a is taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A lumberjack ties the knot with his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered tool for cutting wood, so it is literally a woodcutter.

clue.text: Unfortunately fails to get home in East End

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall out of order
getting something means taking it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the letters of fails rearranged
to be in is to be at home
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone sadly cannot find a home in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: East End looks like the London district, the old working-class area east of the City; split, East gives a letter and End is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To finalise something is to complete it, bringing it to an end.

clue.text: Hangover cure is one of many carried by man's best friend

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a morning drink taken to ease a hangover

definitions.text: one of many carried by man's best friend
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a single strand from a dog's coat

explanation.walkthrough: Man's best friend is the dog, and a dog carries many strands of fur, so the phrase is read word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an alcoholic drink taken to relieve a hangover, from the old notion that like cures like.

clue.text: Awful smell of sulphur by ditch — not right

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: not right tells you the letter standing for right is taken away

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
R is the abbreviation for right; it is removed

explanation.surface: A ditch reeking of sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour.

clue.text: Incite doctor to blow top

indicators.note: blowing your top here means losing the top letter, which in a down entry is the first

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor

explanation.surface: Provoking a doctor until they lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: To blow your top usually means to lose your temper; here it means losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on is to spur or encourage, which is to incite.

clue.text: Chair a Question Time covering Middle East trouble spot

indicators.note: covering means the words hold the solution inside them

parts.note: inside chaIR A Question

explanation.surface: An invitation to host Question Time, the BBC debate show, on a Middle East crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern country that has seen repeated war and conflict.

clue.text: Western hero, after good turn, goes north on freight train

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or discipline it, so the letters are put into a new form

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a U-turn, so turn gives U
N is the abbreviation for north
the letters of freight rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero turns north and boards a freight train.
explanation.walkthrough: Freight train reads as one noun, but train is the signal working on freight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfighter is the classic gunslinging protagonist of a cowboy film.

clue.text: Little bit of criticism snootily expressed?

indicators.note: expressed tells you to say the word out loud, in a posh accent

parts.note: flak is criticism; in a very plummy accent the vowel shifts

explanation.surface: A mild jab of criticism delivered in a stuck-up voice.
explanation.walkthrough: In an exaggerated upper-class English accent the short a of flak drifts towards a short e.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleck is a small spot or particle, a tiny bit of something.

clue.text: Toil away at a PC?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to work slowly and steadily
second meaning: British slang for a police constable

explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer to toil at, but it is a police constable; the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to work doggedly, and Plod is a jokey British name for an ordinary policeman.

clue.text: Artist's static composition nevertheless has vitality

parts.note: still can mean nevertheless
life is liveliness or vitality

explanation.surface: An artist's motionless arrangement that still manages to feel lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of arranged inanimate objects, a static composition.

clue.text: Egg on relative to lose pound in weight

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
L, from libra, is the pound sign; it is removed

explanation.surface: Urging a family member to shed a pound of body weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg on looks like the verb to encourage, but the egg gives a letter and on places it before the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit of weight, a sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Cajole chap into married life that's hollow

indicators.note: something hollow has had its middle emptied, so only the outside letters stay
into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: wed means married
a chap is a he
life with its middle removed

explanation.surface: Coaxing a man into a married life that feels empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax or persuade by flattery, the same as to cajole.

clue.text: Tick off chicken as food produced here

definitions.note: a description of a place; the answer is that place

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of tick rearranged
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Checking off a chicken from the menu as it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick off reads as a phrase meaning reprimand, but off is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is the room where meals are cooked and prepared.
